brief.headline: Push for a 10–15% price cut: they keep 5.9% profit vs peers' 3.8% — room exists, and we have two strong alternates ready.

priceAsk.summary: Ask for a 10–15% price reduction across rigid plastic packaging.
priceAsk.target: Target caps at ₹0.65–0.80/pc (currently market ask is ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, with headroom noted to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume)
priceAsk.basis: They keep 5.9% of every ₹100 they sell vs 3.8% for similar firms — that extra 2.1% gives them room to cut price. Market ask shows modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80/pc at higher volume. We spend ₹5.49 Cr/year and can move volume to Mold-Tek or Manjushree if pricing doesn't improve.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Keep current 30 Days After Receipt — do not extend further.

brief.financialLeverage: They are healthy (CRISIL A+ / Stable, 64/100 health score) and profitable, so we can push hard. They keep 5.9% profit vs peers' 3.8% — margin cushion exists. Their cash is stuck for 104d vs 79d for similar firms, meaning cash is tighter for them than peers, but we're only 0.59% of their ₹937.60 Cr revenue — a tiny customer. However, their sales are growing fast (22.1%/yr per the levers), they want volume, and we have two strong alternates (Mold-Tek, Manjushree) — so lead with price and volume commitment, not payment-term concessions.

evidence.point: They keep more profit than peers
Their cash is stuck longer than similar firms
We are a tiny customer to them
Market asking price shows room to negotiate lower
evidence.figure: ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical, headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume

evidence.point: They pay their own suppliers slower than peers

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, 65/100 health) — pharma bottles, caps, preforms; top second-source candidate per DATA.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹946.50 Cr revenue, 73/100 health) — pails, containers, pharma packaging; robust and profitable alternate.

risks: We're only 0.59% of their revenue (₹5.49 Cr of ₹937.60 Cr) — very small leverage from volume alone; lean on the alternates and their profit cushion instead.

Their finances sit in the grey zone (Altman Z 2.17) — not distress, but not rock-solid either. Push on price, but don't squeeze so hard we destabilize a sole supplier before the alternates are qualified.
Market ask data is for a 28 mm induction-wad PP cap at ₹0.85–0.95/pc typical — confirm our actual SKU specs and volumes match that reference before citing the ₹0.65–0.80 target in the room.

They borrow money at about 12.19% and their cash is stuck for 104d — offering faster payment could unlock a price cut worth roughly that rate, but we should hold payment terms steady (already 30d) and focus the ask on price.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We're here to lock in a long-term partnership on rigid packaging — we want to commit more volume to you, but we need pricing that reflects the 5.9% margin you're making compared to the 3.8% your peers earn, and we've got two strong alternates if we can't close that gap.
